elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Amended Para 27.1 now states: "This Agreement is governed by New York law, with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County." That is an affirmative choice of law where the Agreement previously designated none.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence confers "exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County," and the drafter deleted both the Committee's power to "determine the method, such as arbitration" and the "sole and exclusive remedy" sentence, so no competing arbitral or foreign merits forum survives. No broader alternate-forum carve-out was added; the absence of a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out does not defeat the element, which only permits (does not require) that narrow exception.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The operative language selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. Not met at this level (the preferred level is satisfied instead).

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The forum is the state and federal courts in New York County; no Delaware, California, or London forum is designated. Not met at this level (the preferred level is satisfied instead).

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: both preferred elements are met in operative text (New York law; exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County). The fallback level is not met, which is immaterial because one complete level suffices.

Deviation classification is supportable: the original Agreement designated no governing law (Para 27.2 only excludes facts from a later choice-of-law inquiry) and made a Management Committee determination — expressly including possible arbitration with no stated seat — the "sole and exclusive remedy," failing the fallback on both law and forum and sitting near walk-away.

Minimality holds. Only two deletions were made beyond the inserted sentence, and both are necessary to reach element 2: the Committee's power to "determine the method, such as arbitration" (a competing, potentially foreign-seated forum) and the "sole and exclusive remedy" sentence (which would displace the exclusive court forum). Favourable retained language survives — the reasonable-efforts step, the Committee as a resolution step, the continued-performance sentence, and Para 27.2 are all intact, and no extras (fee-shifting, jury waiver, service-of-process, survival tails) were added.

Intent is preserved on the whole: allocation, timing, and the continued-performance mechanic are unaffected, and Para 27.2 is now largely surplus but not contradictory — it addresses only how an unresolved choice-of-law question would be decided and does not override an express choice.

Residual drafting point (not an element failure, but worth a conforming tweak): Paragraph 20's trigger — "In the event that the Management Committee decides to go to arbitration in accordance with Paragraph 27" — can no longer occur once the Committee's arbitration-election power is removed, leaving that privilege reservation inert. If the counterparty raises it, either conform Paragraph 20's opening to "In any action or proceeding between or among the Parties" or note that the reservation simply lies dormant; do not reinstate the arbitration election in Paragraph 27.
No second flag risk: the redline touches only jurisdiction and forum words and does not re-cut any other commercial term.
